45e257ec05b20651b276f711f560b3c9045fabd9
cli: surface LEGACY_META_ADDRESS instead of a generic INVALID_INPUT

chainBoundary turned every chain-package error into INVALID_INPUT, so a
recipient in a retired format (gpsol: for Solana, st:eth:0x for TRON)
only saw "chain input or evidence is invalid." and never the one fix:
ask for the current meta-address. A SolanaStealthError or TronError with
code LEGACY_META_ADDRESS now keeps that code (fail, exit 1, usual JSON
error shape) and carries the library's fixed message, which never embeds
caller input. Every other chain error stays generic.

a156ee13f5a3bd3978b8e5eb8bcfca2485a0a1a1
cli: report the Solana recipient cluster and refuse mainnet

chain recipient inspect --family solana accepted a meta-address for any
cluster, mainnet included, and reported network: null. It now reports the
decoded cluster (devnet, testnet or localnet) in network, as the Bitcoin
branch does, and refuses a mainnet meta-address with CHAIN_DISABLED
(unsupported, exit 5), the code the CLI already uses for disabled chains:
experimental chains are testnet-only.

a8a7f9d9997e2c6fe5b6829176671144eead99da
chain-tron: fail closed in build() until the GPT1 memo can be bound

ADR-0019 puts the "GPT1" || R || viewTag announcement in the payment
transaction's own raw_data.data, and the web scanner reads the memo only
from the hashed raw_data_hex. build() returned the memo next to a
triggersmartcontract body that cannot carry it, so a request broadcast as
returned paid a stealth address the receiver could never detect. This
package has no local Transaction.raw encoder to bind it, so build() now
throws TronAdapterError MEMO_NOT_BOUND before deriving anything.
buildPaymentRequest checks amount and fee_limit up front, since build()
no longer reaches the TRC-20 builder's checks. No caller outside this
package uses the adapter (the CLI only imports parseTronAddress).

d664c48fbd449371e4d418e56306a7083136b66d
chain-tron: adopt the ADR-0019 st:trx:0x meta-address and GPT1 memo (TB-08)

chain-tron took core-crypto st:eth:0x meta-addresses for TRON, while the
web app (@ghostpay/tron-adapter, ADR-0019 section 2) issues st:trx:0x, so
neither side accepted the other's string. New src/meta.ts reimplements
the tron-adapter codec over core-crypto (same accept set, lowercase
canonical form) and the GPT1 || R || viewTag memo; deriveTronStealthPayment
and the adapter now take st:trx:0x and return the memo. st:eth:0x is
refused with LEGACY_META_ADDRESS: it is the EVM meta-address and need not
belong to the recipient's TRON keys.

src/interop.test.ts checks this package and the tron-adapter source
against test-vectors/meta-address-sol-tron-v1.json and the web package's
test-vectors/tron.json, plus random cross round trips (each side's
payment is detected by the other's scanner).

b46b886eb787e39aafcb8ebd339d09a8d6e56305
chain-solana: adopt the ADR-0017 formats shipped by the web app (TB-08)

chain-solana (imported by the CLI) used gpsol: base58check meta-addresses,
a [8]-cofactor derivation with its own tweak/view-tag hashes and gpst1:
base64url memos. For the same S, V and r it derived a different one-time
address than @ghostpay/solana-stealth, so a CLI-side payer would pay an
address the web wallet never detects. ADR-0017 sections 3 and 5 define
the scheme and the web app ships it, so this package now follows it:

- meta-address st:sol: + base58(0x01 || cluster || S || V || checksum4),
  cluster bound; gpsol: refused with LEGACY_META_ADDRESS, S == V still
  refused (KEY_REUSE); decodeMetaAddress(text, cluster) -> NETWORK_MISMATCH
- Z = r*V, h = SHA-512(dst(shared) || R || Z || S), view tag
  SHA-256(dst(view-tag) || R || Z)[0]
- memo gpst1: + base58(R || view tag); metadata refused, not dropped
- adapter binds meta-addresses to its chain id's cluster

src/interop.test.ts checks this package and the solana-stealth source
against test-vectors/meta-address-sol-tron-v1.json and
test-vectors/solana-stealth.json, plus random cross round trips. The
self-generated vectors and BigInt reference follow ADR-0017.

7060943be540783ffaf4a0203d2a5c83d980742a
Add TB-08 shared Solana and TRON meta-address vectors

test-vectors/meta-address-sol-tron-v1.json pins the formats the web app
ships: the ADR-0017 st:sol: meta-address (10 valid, 23 invalid incl. the
retired gpsol: form, 2 cluster mismatches, 1 documented S == V case),
3 payments with gpst1: base58 memos and 8 invalid memos; the ADR-0019
st:trx:0x meta-address (3 valid, 1 non-canonical accepted, 14 invalid
incl. the st:eth:0x form) and 2 payments with GPT1 memos.

The generator imports only @ghostpay/solana-stealth, @ghostpay/tron-adapter
and @ghostpay/core-crypto (built dist), never the CLI-side packages under
test, and self-checks every vector against the web decoders.
